thread:
incident-bot: [PAGE] High 5xx rate detected from eu-central-1 az1a inference ELB pool. Error spikes started ~1768509100. Affected: model-serving-prod-elb-az1a, ~20% 5xx across p50-p95; routing fallback engaged 8% of requests. Pager: @Mike H @Sana P

Mike H: seeing it, console shows increased target unhealthy for a subset of instances in az1a. Logs full of TLS handshake errors + ENI resets. Confirming whether it's network or instance-level.

Sana P: I'm on it. Reproducing with curl against NLB targets: a few targets return 504, some return 200. Trying instance-level syslogs now.

Dave R: adding context — we got an automated Route53 health-check failover kick for a handful of records earlier. Could be partial DNS propagation + some instances flapping.

Mike H: @Dave R interesting — traffic steer kicked in. Seeing consistent 200 for failover endpoints but error rate for az1a still ~18%. Customers calling: increased latency and intermittent 502/504s on embeddings endpoints.

Jen L: started an on-call handoff note: "az1a partial network/instance degradation affecting inference ELB — steering in progress, escalation to cloud if nodes keep flapping."

Kai T: quick triage commands I ran:
```
# check unhealthy targets
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | select(.TargetHealth.State=="unhealthy")'
# verify instance ENI states
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=eu-central-1a Name=status,Values=available,associated
```
One node shows repeated ENI detach/attach events in cloudtrail.

Sana P: got the instance syslog: repeated "eni reset" messages + iptables conntrack errors. Also seeing kernel messages about lro/gro timeouts. Suspect host NIC driver or hypervisor network plane.

Mike H: mitigation plan: 1) immediate: increase Route53 failover weight for other AZs to 90% for affected routes (reduce pressure on az1a). 2) cordon & drain unhealthy nodes in az1a serving pool. 3) open ticket with AWS for ENI/hypervisor network investigation. Anyone object?

Dave R: +1. Doing Route53 change now (low TTL update). Note: need to ensure Dedicated customers pinned to az1a are unaffected — ping @prod-ops to confirm re-routing policy is ok.

Jen L: I'll message Prod-ops and Sales SRE to confirm high-commit customers. Also logging customer-impact note in incident tracker.

incident-bot: [ACTION] Route53 change-request submitted (change-id Z3ABC...) TTL reduced to 30s.

Kai T: draining nodes in k8s behind inference autoscaling group. Command: `kubectl drain inference-node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting now.

Sana P: one node failed to drain cleanly — pods stuck terminating (stuck on persistent cache unmount). For low-latency customer-facing pods, enabling graceful shutdown override to speed eviction.

Mike H: monitoring 5xx after initial steering — dropped from 18% to ~6% in 5m. P50 latency back to baseline for most customers, but embeddings throughput still throttled for some high-QPS tenants.

Dave R: AWS ticket opened (case 123456789). Support acknowledges possible host-level networking issue and requested instance IDs + time window. Sharing CloudTrail + ENI event logs now.

Jen L: posting status to #customers-impacted channel: brief summary, affected regions, mitigation steps, ETA unknown, contact for urgent escalation.

Sana P: continuing to replace flapping instances with fresh capacity (ASG replace-instances). Confirmed new instances attach ENIs and serve cleanly. Rolling replacement at 2 instances/min to avoid capacity crunch.

Mike H: action checklist:
- [x] Route53 failover weight adjust (30s TTL)
- [x] k8s drain and ASG replace for flapping hosts
- [x] AWS support case opened
- [ ] run traffic soak test on restored nodes (Kai)
- [ ] resume normal weights when stable for 15m

Kai T: will run soot tests and synthetic traffic against new nodes, and validate KV cache priming. Script I'm using: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://inference.example/api/generate?model=redwood-3 | jq '.tokens' > /dev/null
  sleep 0.05
done
```
Early run shows stable responses from replaced nodes.

Dave R: AWS support updated: they observed hypervisor NIC counters spike, possible underlying host NIC fault. They recommended evacuating instances on the affected hosts and offered to migrate. They've scheduled a host maintenance window in 2h.

Sana P: recommended next steps: keep failover weights high, continue replacing flapping instances, and avoid rolling upgrades in eu-central-1a until AWS finishes maintenance.

Mike H: agreed. I'll keep on-call for next 2 hours then handoff to Jen. Leaving a note: watch for DNS propagation anomalies once we lower weights — TTL 30s helps but monitor at edge.

Jen L: taking over on-call at 1768510800. I'll run customer impact sweep and coordinate with account teams for any affected Dedicated customers.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] error rate below threshold for 15m; automated alert cleared, but humans marked incident "degraded" until host maintenance completes.

Mike H: final notes for postmortem: capture timeline of ENI resets, ASG replace counts, Route53 changes + exact customer list impacted, and consider automating faster AZ steering for inference routes when health-checks detect ENI flaps.

Jen L: will open incident ticket in JIRA and add action items: (1) evaluate autoscaler backoff when ENI flaps, (2) postmortem with AWS support logs, (3) doc for customer comms template.

Kai T: thumbs up. Anything else?

Mike H: nothing else. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
